attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: other series of legends on primitive history, including the story of the building of the Tower of Babel and of the Confusion of Tongues.

canonical_statement: The universe originated from a state of primordial chaos or confusion.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: The narrative on the Assyrian tablets commences with a description of the period before the world was created, when there existed a chaos or confusion.

canonical_statement: Primordial chaos is associated with the generation of monstrous entities.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: The desolate and empty state of the universe and the generation by chaos of monsters are vividly given.

canonical_statement: A female entity presides over the state of primordial chaos.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: The chaos is presided over by a female power named Tisalat and Tiamat...

canonical_statement: A celestial being, analogous to Satan, fell due to ambition, raising opposition against the divine authority.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: We are told, in the inscriptions, of the fall of the celestial being who appears to correspond to Satan. In his ambition he raises his hand against the sanctuary of the God of heaven...

canonical_statement: The universe was created in stages by divine beings.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: the gods in due course creating the universe in stages

canonical_statement: Humanity was created by divine beings.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: The divine work culminates in the creation of man

canonical_statement: Humanity was created in an upright state, free from evil.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: man, who is made upright and free from evil

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses the faculty of speech as a divine endowment.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: endowed by the gods with the noble faculty of speech

canonical_statement: Humanity's initial state of blessing was lost due to temptation and subsequent fall.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: man, yielding to temptation, falls; and the Deity then pronounces upon him a terrible curse

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives exist that describe the origin of the world, the creation of life, the fall from a sinless state, and cosmic conflicts between divine and evil forces.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: A long account of the origin of the world, the creation of the animals and man, the fall of man from a sinless state, and a conflict between the gods and the powers of evil.

canonical_statement: Multiple ancient accounts of creation exist, some of which exhibit close correspondence with each other.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: A second account of the creation having a closer correspondence with the account of Berosus.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives describe the existence and history of evil spirits, sometimes as part of creation accounts.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: A Bilingual legend of the history of the seven evil spirits, apparently part of a third version of the creation.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives include stories of deities descending into and returning from an underworld or Hades.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Story of the descent of the goddess Ishtar or Venus into Hades, and her return.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives depict deities engaging in actions considered sinful, such as insulting other gods.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Legend of the sin of the God Zu, who insults Elu, the father of the gods.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives describe deities associated with specific phenomena, such as pestilence.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Collection of five tablets giving the exploits of Lubara the god of the pestilence.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives include accounts of deities undergoing transformations, such as changing into animals.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Legend of the god Sarturda, who turned into a bird.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives contain stories about wise individuals posing challenges or riddles to deities.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Story of the wise man who put forth a riddle to the gods.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives contrast the goodness of certain individuals with the pervasive wickedness of the world.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Legend of the good man Atarpi, and the wickedness of the world.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives describe significant events leading to the dispersion of humanity, such as the building of a tower.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Legend of the tower of Babel, and dispersion.

canonical_statement: Ancient narratives include extensive accounts of a great flood.

attributions.chapter: THE DISCOVERY OF THE GENESIS LEGENDS.
attributions.surface_quote: Izdubar legends: twelve tablets, with the history of Izdubar, and an account of the flood.

canonical_statement: Traditions concerning the creation of the universe and early human history can exist across different cultures and exhibit similarities.

attributions.surface_quote: traditions of the creation of the universe, and human history... existed parallel to, and in some points identical with, those given in the Book of Genesis.

canonical_statement: All phenomena within the natural world are indicative of future occurrences.

attributions.surface_quote: everything in nature is supposed to portend some coming event.

canonical_statement: Historical records can preserve knowledge of cosmic origins and human history over vast timescales.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: writings contained histories of the heaven and of the sea; of the birth of mankind

canonical_statement: The primordial state of existence was characterized by darkness and an abyss of waters.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: There was a time in which there existed nothing but darkness and an abyss of waters.

canonical_statement: Hideous beings were produced from a dualistic principle within the primordial watery abyss.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: wherein resided most hideous beings, which were produced of a two-fold principle.

canonical_statement: Early human forms exhibited diverse and often composite physical characteristics, including multiple limbs, heads, and mixed species features.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: There appeared men, some of whom were furnished with two wings, others with four, and with two faces.

canonical_statement: Some primordial beings possessed both male and female reproductive organs within a single body.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: They had one body, but two heads; the one that of a man, the other of a woman; and likewise in their several organs both male and female.

canonical_statement: The cosmos originated from the division of a primordial feminine entity.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: Belus came, and cut the woman asunder, and of one half of her he formed the earth, and of the other half the heavens

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses rationality and divine knowledge due to its creation from divine blood.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: the deity above-mentioned took off his own head; upon which the other gods mixed the blood...and from thence formed men. On this account it is that they are rational, and partake of divine knowledge.

canonical_statement: A divine being established order in the universe by separating primordial elements.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: Belus, by whom they signify Jupiter, divided the darkness, and separated the heavens from the earth, and reduced the universe to order.

canonical_statement: The current forms of life were created after earlier forms perished due to environmental changes.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: The animals, not being able to bear the prevalence of light, died. Belus upon this...commanded one of the gods to take off his head, and to mix the blood with the earth, and from thence to form other men and animals, which should be capable of bearing the air.

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies were formed by a divine entity.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: Belus formed also the stars, and the sun, and the moon, and the five planets.

canonical_statement: Divine entities communicate with mortals through visions to convey warnings and instructions.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: The deity Cronos appeared to him in a vision, and warned him that upon the fifteenth day... there would be a flood...

canonical_statement: Divine entities possess foreknowledge of future catastrophic events.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: The deity Cronos... warned him that upon the fifteenth day... there would be a flood, by which mankind would be destroyed.

canonical_statement: Divine entities issue commands to mortals regarding actions necessary for survival or preservation.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: He therefore enjoined him to write a history... and to bury it... and to build a vessel, and take with him...

canonical_statement: Mortals can journey to the realm of divine entities after fulfilling divine directives.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: Having asked the Deity whither he was to sail, he was answered, 'To the Gods;'

canonical_statement: Divine beings can elevate pious mortals to their own realm.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: it was upon account of his piety that he was translated to live with the gods

canonical_statement: Mortals can achieve a state of existence among the gods.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: his wife and daughter and the pilot had obtained the same honour

canonical_statement: Divine communication can occur through disembodied voices.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: they could distinguish his voice in the air

canonical_statement: Sacred knowledge is preserved in written form for humanity.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: search for the writings at Sippara, which they were to make known to all mankind

canonical_statement: Divine beings can manifest in physical forms that combine human and animal characteristics.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: appeared again from the Erythraean sea a fourth Annedotus, having the same form with those above, the shape of a fish blended with that of a man.

canonical_statement: Divine appointment can legitimize earthly rulers.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: God had appointed him to be the shepherd of the people

canonical_statement: Time can be measured in units of varying, extensive durations.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: a sarus is esteemed to be three thousand six hundred years, a neros six hundred, and a sossus sixty.

canonical_statement: Divine entities can communicate future events to mortals.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: the deity Cronos foretold that on the fifteenth day...there would be a deluge of rain

canonical_statement: Divine entities can issue commands to mortals.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: he commanded him to deposit all the writings whatever

canonical_statement: Divine entities can directly inspire or influence mortals.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: was presently inspired by God

canonical_statement: Divine entities can elevate mortals from the human state.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: the gods translated him from among men

canonical_statement: The diversity of human languages originated from divine intervention as a consequence of humanity's attempt to ascend to the heavens.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: the gods introduced a diversity of tongues among men, who till that time had all spoken the same language

canonical_statement: Divine entities can intervene in the physical world to thwart human endeavors.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: the winds assisted the gods, and overthrew the work upon its contrivers

canonical_statement: Humanity once shared a single, universal language.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: all men formerly spoke the same language

canonical_statement: Divine beings can alter fundamental aspects of human existence, such as language, as a form of punishment or consequence.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: God sending forth a whirlwind confounded their design, and gave to each tribe a particular language

canonical_statement: The universe originates from two fundamental principles, a masculine and a feminine.

attributions.surface_quote: they constitute two, Tauthe and Apason, making Apason the husband of Tauthe

canonical_statement: The feminine principle is the progenitor of divine entities.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: denominating her the mother of the gods

canonical_statement: The intelligible world is an emanation from the two primary principles.

attributions.chapter: CHALDEAN LEGENDS TRANSMITTED THROUGH BEROSUS AND OTHER ANCIENT AUTHORS.
attributions.surface_quote: Moymis, which I conceive is no other than the intelligible world proceeding from the two principles

canonical_statement: The world was fabricated by a divine entity known as Belus.

attributions.surface_quote: a son called Belus, who, they say, is the fabricator of the world, the Demiurgus

canonical_statement: Mythological systems, initially localized around specific deities and their worship centers, evolve over time into interconnected pantheons.

attributions.surface_quote: Babylonian mythology was local in origin; each of the gods had a particular city which was the seat of his worship, and it is probable that the idea of weaving the gods into a system, in which each should have his part to play, only had its origin at a later time.

canonical_statement: Ancient mythological systems can achieve completion and stability millennia before later historical eras.

attributions.surface_quote: The antiquity of this mythology may be seen by the fact, that two thousand years before the Christian era it was already completed, and its deities definitely connected into a system which remained with little change down to the close of the kingdom.

canonical_statement: The perceived hierarchy and relationships among deities can be influenced by political and social changes in human civilizations.

attributions.surface_quote: Political changes in early times led to the rise and fall of various cities and consequently of their deities

canonical_statement: Deities can be associated with specific domains of influence, powers, and geographical locations.

attributions.surface_quote: Anu, king of angels and spirits, lord of the city of Erech. Bel, lord of the world, creator.

canonical_statement: Deities can retain their established positions within a pantheon even after the decline of their associated human cities.

attributions.surface_quote: Subsequent changes led to the decline of these cities, but their deities still retained their position

canonical_statement: The universe is structured hierarchically with deities at the apex, followed by celestial and terrestrial angels, and then various classes of spirits.

attributions.surface_quote: Below these deities there was a large body of gods... below these were arranged the Igege... and the Anunnaki... Below these again came various classes of spirits.

canonical_statement: Abstract divinity can be personified as an original principle that represents the universe's upper and lower regions.

attributions.surface_quote: Anu represents abstract divinity, and he appears as an original principle... represents the universe as the upper and lower regions.

canonical_statement: The division of the universe into upper and lower regions is associated with a male and female divine principle.

attributions.surface_quote: when these were divided the upper region or heaven was called Anu, while the lower region or earth was called Anatu; Anatu being the female principle or wife of Anu.

canonical_statement: Divine manifestations can emerge from an original chaotic state.

attributions.surface_quote: These forms are said to have sprung out of the original chaos.

canonical_statement: A female divine principle can be a counterpart to a male divine principle, representing contrasting aspects like depth and darkness.

attributions.surface_quote: when Anu represents height and heaven, Anatu represents depth and earth; she is also lady of darkness.

canonical_statement: Deities can be associated with specific natural phenomena or domains of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Vul is god of the region of the atmosphere, or space between the heaven and earth, he is the god of rain, of storms and whirlwind, of thunder and lightning, of floods and watercourses.

canonical_statement: Deities can be known by multiple names across different cultures or contexts.

attributions.surface_quote: The air-god is usually called Vul, he has also the name Pur, and the epithets Ramman or Rimmon... In Syria and Arabia, where he bore the name of Daddi; in Armenia he was called Teiseba.

canonical_statement: Deities can possess the attribute of self-existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Ramman or Rimmon, the self-existent

canonical_statement: Deities can be associated with specific human practices or powers, such as witchcraft.

attributions.surface_quote: The fire-god... is considered to be the most potent deity in relation to witchcraft and spells generally.

canonical_statement: The conceptualization and worship of deities can evolve over time, altering their perceived nature or prominence.

attributions.surface_quote: The first intention in the mythology was only to represent love as heaven-born; but in time a more sensual view prevailed, and the worship of Istar became one of the darkest features in Babylonian mythology.

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies can be identified with specific deities.

attributions.surface_quote: The planet Venus, as the evening star, was identified with the Ishtar of Erech, while the morning star was Anunit, goddess of Akkad.

canonical_statement: Deities can be associated with specific domains of existence, such as the sea, the underworld, or wisdom.

attributions.surface_quote: Hea, who is god of the sea and of Hades, in fact of all the lower regions.

canonical_statement: Deities can have multiple aspects or correspondences to other divine figures across different pantheons.

attributions.surface_quote: He has two features, and corresponds in some respects to the Saturn or Cronos of the ancients.

canonical_statement: Divine beings can be responsible for the generation and existence of human beings.

attributions.surface_quote: he is lord of generation and of all human beings

canonical_statement: Divine beings can act as agents in the process of creation, often under the authority of a higher deity.

attributions.surface_quote: Merodach is an active agent in creation, but is always subordinate to his father Hea.

canonical_statement: The status and prominence of deities within a pantheon can change over time, often influenced by political or cultural shifts.

attributions.surface_quote: In later times, after Babylon had been made the capital, Merodach... was raised to the head of the Pantheon.

canonical_statement: Deities can be associated with specific domains of influence, such as the surface of the earth and human affairs.

attributions.surface_quote: he was lord of the surface of the earth and the affairs of men.

canonical_statement: Deities can have multiple names or titles.

attributions.surface_quote: his names were Enu, Elu, Kaptu, and Bel

canonical_statement: Deities can be associated with specific geographical locations or cities.

attributions.surface_quote: Elu was lord of the city of Nipur

canonical_statement: Deities can have consorts or spouses.

attributions.surface_quote: had a consort named Belat or Beltis

canonical_statement: The prominence of a deity's worship can indicate the historical importance of their associated city.

attributions.surface_quote: extensive worship of Bel...point to a time when his city, Nipur, was the metropolis

canonical_statement: Generic titles for deities can be applied to multiple distinct divine entities.

attributions.surface_quote: title Belat was only 'lady,' or 'goddess,' it was a common one for many goddesses

canonical_statement: Deities can have offspring.

attributions.surface_quote: Elu had, like the other gods, a numerous family; his eldest son was the moon-god

canonical_statement: The relative importance of celestial bodies in a mythological system can determine the hierarchy of their associated deities.

attributions.surface_quote: In the Babylonian system the moon takes precedence of the sun

canonical_statement: Deities with the same name can be considered distinct entities if associated with different locations.

attributions.surface_quote: Shamas of Larsa was probably considered a different deity to Shamas of Sippara

canonical_statement: The primordial state of existence was an undifferentiated chaos or void.

attributions.surface_quote: When above, were not raised the heavens: and below on the earth a plant had not grown up; the abyss also had not broken open their boundaries

canonical_statement: A primordial entity, Tiamat, was the generative source of all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: The chaos (or water) Tiamat (the sea) was the producing-mother of the whole of them.

canonical_statement: Order did not exist in the primordial state before the emergence of the gods.

attributions.surface_quote: When the gods had not sprung up, any one of them; a plant had not grown, and order did not exist;

canonical_statement: The initial state of existence before creation was a chaotic void.

attributions.surface_quote: description of the chaos or desolate void before the Creation of the world

canonical_statement: The sea is the primordial substance from which all things originated.

attributions.surface_quote: the sea was the origin of all things

canonical_statement: Divine beings were created in a sequential process.

attributions.surface_quote: Were made also the great gods, the gods Lahmu and Lahamu they caused to come

canonical_statement: The universe originated from a primordial watery chaos.

attributions.surface_quote: a watery chaos preceded the creation, and formed, in fact, the origin and groundwork of the universe.

canonical_statement: Deities can be personifications of fundamental cosmic principles like motion and production.

attributions.surface_quote: Lahma or Lahmu, and Lahama or Lahamu; these are male and female personifications of motion and production

canonical_statement: The cosmos is structured into distinct upper and lower expanses.

attributions.surface_quote: Sar or Ilsar, and Kisar, representing the upper expanse and the lower expanse

canonical_statement: Specific deities embody fundamental cosmic domains such as heaven, earth, and sea.

attributions.surface_quote: Anu represents the heaven, Elu the earth, and Hea the sea, in this new form of the universe.

canonical_statement: The universe is formed through the combination of male and female principles.

attributions.surface_quote: In each case there appears to be a male and female principle, which principles combine in the formation of the universe.

canonical_statement: The celestial bodies were intentionally arranged by divine entities.

attributions.surface_quote: It was delightful, all that was fixed by the great gods. Stars, their appearance he arranged.

canonical_statement: The arrangement of stars serves to delineate temporal cycles.

attributions.surface_quote: To fix the year through the observation of their constellations, twelve months he arranged.

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies possess specific, divinely ordained courses.

attributions.surface_quote: He marked the positions of the wandering stars to shine in their courses.

canonical_statement: The moon god Uru was caused to emerge from primordial chaos to illuminate the night.

attributions.surface_quote: In its mass (i.e. the lower chaos) he made a boiling, the god Uru he caused to rise out, the night he overshadowed, to fix it also for the light of the night.

canonical_statement: The moon's phases are a regular, divinely established cycle.

attributions.surface_quote: That the month might not be broken, and in its amount be regular. At the beginning of the month, at the rising of the night, his horns are breaking through to shine on the heaven. On the seventh day to a circle he begins to swell.

canonical_statement: The creation of celestial bodies, such as the sun and moon, is a distinct stage in the formation of the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: the appointment of the heavenly orbs. It parallels the fourth day of Creation in the first chapter of Genesis

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies are established to provide light, mark time, and govern day and night.

attributions.surface_quote: Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years

canonical_statement: The creation process is structured into distinct phases, each corresponding to a 'day' or tablet.

attributions.surface_quote: the events of each of the days of Genesis were recorded on a separate tablet

canonical_statement: The creation of the universe was a process of divine arrangement and satisfaction.

attributions.surface_quote: previous creations were "delightful," or satisfactory, agreeing with the oft-repeated statement of Genesis

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies are arranged in specific courses and serve as markers for time and events.

attributions.surface_quote: stars were set in courses to point out the year... heavenly bodies gave... signs of events

canonical_statement: The positions and appearances of celestial bodies provide omens for earthly occurrences.

attributions.surface_quote: heavenly bodies gave, by their appearance and positions, signs of events which were coming on the earth

canonical_statement: The cosmos is structured into distinct heavenly divisions, each associated with specific deities.

attributions.surface_quote: Anu, god of the heavens, was considered to be the creator of the heavenly hosts; for it is he who shares with Bel and Hea the divisions of the face of the sky.

canonical_statement: The world was formed from primordial waters and rests upon a chaotic oceanic abyss.

attributions.surface_quote: They evidently considered that the world was drawn together out of the waters, and rested or reposed upon a vast abyss of chaotic ocean which filled the space below the world.

canonical_statement: A dark, infernal lake, contained by gates, exists beneath the world.

attributions.surface_quote: This dark infernal lake was shut in by gigantic gates and strong fastenings, which prevented the floods from overwhelming the world.

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies can be created through divine manipulation of primordial chaos.

attributions.surface_quote: When the deity decided to create the moon, he is represented as drawing aside the gates of this abyss, and creating a whirling motion like boiling in the dark ocean below; then, at his bidding, from this turmoil, arose the moon like a giant bubble...

canonical_statement: Celestial bodies follow divinely ordained paths and functions.

attributions.surface_quote: The Babylonian account continues with the regulation of the motions of the moon to overshadow the night, to regulate and give light until the dawn of day.

canonical_statement: The moon is considered a principal celestial body, created before the sun.

canonical_statement: Divine entities can intervene in human experience to provide solace or guidance.

attributions.surface_quote: into the presence of the gods came my supplication; and they sent peace unto me.

canonical_statement: Reality contains beings of composite form that bridge different cosmic realms.

attributions.surface_quote: composite monsters with their feet resting in hell, and their heads reaching heaven.

canonical_statement: Certain beings have a function in the cosmic order, such as guiding celestial bodies.

attributions.surface_quote: These beings are supposed to guide and direct the sun at its rising and setting.

canonical_statement: Death and destruction are inherent aspects of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Spoiling and death together exist

canonical_statement: The form or image of death is imperceptible or unknown.

attributions.surface_quote: of death the image has not been seen

canonical_statement: Divine beings guide individuals at the moment of death.

attributions.surface_quote: the spirit of the great gods takes his hand

canonical_statement: A specific deity, Mamitu, is responsible for determining individual destinies.

attributions.surface_quote: The goddess Mamitu maker of fate, to them their fate brings

canonical_statement: The goddess Mamitu has established the fundamental conditions of life and death.

attributions.surface_quote: she has fixed death and life

canonical_statement: The precise timing of an individual's death is unknowable.

attributions.surface_quote: of death the day is not known

canonical_statement: A realm of death exists, separate from the mortal world.

attributions.surface_quote: waters of death which separated the abode of Hasisadra from the world of mortals

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess the authority to determine the fate of cities and their inhabitants, including their destruction.

attributions.surface_quote: The city Surippak...that city is ancient....the gods within it...their will he revealed...I destroy? the sinner

canonical_statement: Divine beings communicate their will and intentions to mortals.

attributions.surface_quote: their will he revealed...I his will was hearing and he spake to me

canonical_statement: Divine beings can command mortals to undertake specific actions to avert or survive divine judgment.

attributions.surface_quote: make a ship after this...cause to go in? the seed of life all of it to the midst of the ship.

canonical_statement: Divine beings can orchestrate the gathering of all forms of life for preservation.

attributions.surface_quote: the beasts of the field, the animals of the field all, I will gather and I will send to thee

canonical_statement: Divine entities can directly influence and orchestrate natural phenomena, such as floods.

attributions.surface_quote: A flood Shamas made and he spake saying in the night: I will cause it to rain heavily

canonical_statement: Divine entities communicate their intentions and commands to mortals.

attributions.surface_quote: he spake saying in the night: I will cause it to rain heavily, enter to the midst of the ship and shut thy door.

canonical_statement: Multiple divine entities can participate in and contribute to a single significant event.

attributions.surface_quote: Vul in the midst of it thundered, and Nebo and Saru went in front, the throne bearers went over mountains and plains, the destroyer Nergal overturned, Ninip went in front and cast down, the spirits carried destruction

canonical_statement: Divine actions can result in the transformation of the physical world, such as turning fertile land into a wasteland.

attributions.surface_quote: The bright earth to a waste was turned

canonical_statement: Divine beings can experience fear and seek refuge from natural phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: the gods feared the tempest and sought refuge; they ascended to the heaven of Anu.

canonical_statement: Prophecy is a foretelling of future events, including catastrophic ones.

attributions.surface_quote: I in the presence of the gods prophesied evil. As I prophesied... to evil were devoted all my people

canonical_statement: Divine beings can experience sorrow and lament over the fate of mortals.

attributions.surface_quote: The gods concerning the spirits were weeping with her, the gods in seats seated in lamentation

canonical_statement: Humanity is susceptible to complete destruction and corruption.

attributions.surface_quote: the whole of mankind turned to corruption, like reeds the corpses floated.

canonical_statement: Divine beings are attracted to and sustained by offerings.

attributions.surface_quote: The gods collected at its savour, the gods collected at its good savour; the gods like flies over the sacrifice gathered.

canonical_statement: A divine entity created a fundamental cosmic element.

attributions.surface_quote: Rubat in her course The great brightness of Anu had created.

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess the capacity to initiate catastrophic events, such as deluges, as a form of judgment or punishment.

attributions.surface_quote: when thou art angry a deluge thou makest

canonical_statement: Divine judgment can be disproportionate, punishing the innocent alongside the guilty.

attributions.surface_quote: the just prince let him not be cut off, the faithful let him not be destroyed

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess the ability to grant immortality or a god-like state to mortals.

attributions.surface_quote: to be like the gods are carried away; then shall dwell Hasisadra in a remote place

canonical_statement: Divine beings can communicate their judgments or intentions to mortals through dreams.

attributions.surface_quote: Adrahasis a dream they sent, and the judgment of the gods he heard

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess omniscience.

attributions.surface_quote: Hea knew all things

canonical_statement: Physical ailments can be transmuted into health and beauty through ritualistic cleansing with water.

attributions.surface_quote: his disease in the water to beauty may it turn, may he cast off his illness, and the sea carry it away

canonical_statement: Divine or ancient beings possess hidden knowledge and judgments that can be revealed to mortals.

attributions.surface_quote: Be revealed to thee Izdubar the concealed story; and the judgment of the gods be related to thee.

canonical_statement: The earth is a final destination or state of being after death.

attributions.surface_quote: The arms of the earth have taken thee.

canonical_statement: Darkness is a maternal entity or a state associated with a maternal deity.

attributions.surface_quote: O darkness, O darkness, mother Ninazu, O darkness.

canonical_statement: The earth has the power to claim individuals, even when other forces or entities do not.

attributions.surface_quote: Simtar did not take him, Asakku did not take him, the earth took him.

canonical_statement: The earth can inflict a 'sting' or 'deadly wound' upon an individual.

attributions.surface_quote: a sting to the earth has struck me, a deadly wound to the earth has struck me

canonical_statement: The spirit of a deceased individual can ascend from the earth.

attributions.surface_quote: the spirit (or ghost) of Heabani ... from the earth arose

canonical_statement: Religious narratives are shaped by the cultural and geographical context of the people who create them.

attributions.surface_quote: each nation should colour them in accordance with its own ideas

canonical_statement: The concept of divinity varies significantly across different cultures and belief systems.

attributions.surface_quote: total difference between the religious ideas of the two peoples, the Jews believing in one God... while the Babylonians worshipped gods and lords many

canonical_statement: The soul can be confined to the earthly plane after death if it is not accepted into designated afterlife regions.

attributions.surface_quote: The soul of Heabani was confined to the earth, and, not resting there, intercession was made to transfer him to the region of the blessed.

canonical_statement: There are distinct regions in the afterlife, some for bliss and some for joy, which souls may or may not be admitted to.

attributions.surface_quote: The Babylonians had two separate regions for a future state, one of bliss, the other of joy.

canonical_statement: The names of certain antediluvian patriarchs correspond to Babylonian words and roots, suggesting a linguistic or conceptual connection.

attributions.surface_quote: Several of the other names of antediluvian patriarchs correspond with Babylonian words and roots

canonical_statement: The name 'Adam' in ancient creation legends refers to 'man' in a general sense, not as a specific proper name.

attributions.surface_quote: The name Adam is in the Creation legends, but only in a general sense as man, not as a proper name.

canonical_statement: Tribal migrations in early times could lead to the transfer of geographical names to new settlements.

attributions.surface_quote: In early times tribes often migrated and carried their geographical names to their new homes

canonical_statement: The name 'Lamech' is associated with a deified Phoenician patriarch and forms of a name for the moon in cuneiform texts.

attributions.surface_quote: Lamech has already been pointed out... in the name of the Deified Phoenician patriarch Diamich; this name is found... as Dumugu and Lamga, two forms of a name of the moon.

canonical_statement: The figure of Tubal Cain, as a metal worker, corresponds in name and character to the deity Vulcan and a Babylonian god of fire and metalworking.

attributions.surface_quote: Tubal Cain, the father or instructor of all metal workers, has been compared with the name of Vulcan... The corresponding deity in Babylonian mythology... has a name formed of two characters which read Bil-kan.

canonical_statement: Events and actions, once performed, tend to recur or be repeated in subsequent manifestations of reality.

attributions.surface_quote: every action, when once performed, has a tendency to be repeated.

canonical_statement: The origin of all things is a primordial chaos, a spirit of confusion and darkness, which predates even the gods.

attributions.surface_quote: the original chaos, the spirit of confusion and darkness, which was the origin of all things, and which was even older than the gods.

canonical_statement: The presence of evil in the world originates from the primordial chaos.

attributions.surface_quote: they accounted for the great problem of humanity--the presence of evil in the world--by making out that it proceeded from the original chaos

canonical_statement: Existence originated from a primordial state of watery chaos.

attributions.surface_quote: there was a chaos of watery matter before the Creation, and from this all things were generated.

canonical_statement: The cosmos, including celestial bodies, was intentionally created by divine entities.

attributions.surface_quote: God created the constellations of the stars, the signs of the zodiac, the planets or wandering stars, the moon and tine sun.

canonical_statement: Humanity was created in a state of perfection and given religious duties.

attributions.surface_quote: mankind, called Adam, as in the Bible; he is made perfect, and instructed in his various religious duties

canonical_statement: A primordial conflict exists between forces of good (gods) and forces of evil/chaos (dragon of the deep).

attributions.surface_quote: war between the dragon and powers of evil, or chaos on one side and the gods on the other.

canonical_statement: The principles of good ultimately triumph over the principles of evil.

attributions.surface_quote: The war... ends of course in the triumph of the principles of good

canonical_statement: Celestial beings interacted with Earth's inhabitants in a significant period preceding a global flood.

attributions.surface_quote: celestial visitors came backwards and forwards to the earth, and the inhabitants of the world were very clearly divided into the good and bad

canonical_statement: A global flood event marks a foundational transition point for the 'modern world' in historical narratives.

attributions.surface_quote: the Flood becomes the starting point for the modern world in both histories

canonical_statement: The concept of a global flood is a shared event across distinct historical and religious accounts.

attributions.surface_quote: both the Bible and the Babylonian story describe the same event

canonical_statement: Civilization, including advanced arts like writing, existed prior to a global flood event.

attributions.surface_quote: several of the Babylonian cities were built before the Flood, and various arts were known, including writing

canonical_statement: Humanity was created.

attributions.surface_quote: Man, creation of, <page 77>, <page 78>.

canonical_statement: Humanity experienced a fall from a prior state.

attributions.surface_quote: fall of, <page 83>-<page 87>.

canonical_statement: The moon was created.

attributions.surface_quote: Moon, creation of, <page 70>.
